access_count.description: Number of recalls that have returned this record. A record with many accesses and no supersession is load-bearing; a record with zero after its decay window is a forgetting candidate.

confidence.description: How much the agent believes this record is true. Direct observation is high; inference from a single episode is low. Recall can filter on a minimum.

content.description: Natural-language surface form. This is the text that gets embedded, keyword-indexed, and injected into a host prompt. Everything a reader needs should be here; payload is for machines.

embedding_model.description: Identifier of the model that produced this record's vector. Required to detect drift when the embedder changes and to schedule a re-embed pass.

expires_at.description: Hard expiry. The daemon tombstones the record once passed. Null means no TTL.

id.description: Stable primary key. Assigned by the memory agent, never by the host.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-supplied key, unique within a scope. A repeated write with the same key returns the original record instead of creating a duplicate. This is what makes the agent safe inside a retrying loop.

importance.description: How much this record should be favoured independent of query relevance. Assigned by the writer, optionally revised by reflection.

last_accessed_at.description: Set every time this record is returned by a recall. Drives the recency term in the retrieval score.

payload.description: Structured, type-specific or host-specific data. Never embedded, never keyword-indexed. Opaque to the memory agent.

schema_version.description: Contract version this record was written against. Bumped only on breaking changes.

scope.description: Namespace isolating one agent, project, or tenant from another. Recall never crosses a scope unless explicitly asked to. Use dotted segments for hierarchy, e.g. 'leewood.crm.builder'.

superseded_by.description: When a newer record replaces this one, the newer record's id. Set together with status='superseded'.

tags.description: Free-form labels for filtering. Lowercase, no spaces.

type.description: Which CoALA long-term memory module this record belongs to.

provenance.description: Where this record came from. Non-negotiable for semantic records: a fact with no traceable origin cannot be adjudicated when it later contradicts something.

agent.description: Identifier of the writing agent or orchestration, e.g. 'crm-builder' or 'memory-agent.daemon'.

derived_from.description: Record ids this one was distilled from. A semantic fact produced by reflection points back at the episodes that produced it.

source.description: host = written by an attached orchestration. daemon = written by the independent consolidation loop. human = written or approved by a person. import = bulk-seeded from an external corpus.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Only 'active' records are returned by recall. Nothing is ever silently destroyed: forgetting moves a record to 'tombstoned' or 'redacted' so the audit trail survives.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 timestamp, always UTC with an explicit offset.

description: Fields common to every long-term memory record, regardless of CoALA memory module. Episodic, semantic, and procedural records all extend this envelope. Note: $id values are stable identifiers, not fetchable URLs; $refs are relative and resolve against the file layout.
title: Memory Envelope
